mainTopic: End of איזהו נשך: the scope of רבית, who violates it, and proper conduct in lending. Then the opening משנה of השוכר את האומנין on workers who back out.
overview: This amud finishes the chapter איזהו נשך and begins a new chapter. The משנה teaches that neighbors who swap plowing days must keep the swap within one season. רבן גמליאל adds that a gift given before a loan or after it is repaid is still רבית, and רבי שמעון says that even helpful words can be רבית. The משנה then lists everyone in a רבית loan who breaks a לא תעשה, and אביי explains which of the five לאוים each person breaks. The גמרא adds that even a greeting can be רבית, that lenders of רבית lose more than they gain, and that a lender may not pressure a borrower who cannot pay. רב and ריש לקיש warn against lending without witnesses, and the story of רבינא and רב אשי shows this rule kept even with a great scholar. After the הדרן, the new chapter השוכר את האומנין opens with rules about workers and employers who mislead each other or back out of a job.

steps.title: Swapping plowing days must stay within one season
steps.stepSummary: Days within the dry season count as equal, and days within the rainy season count as equal. But a dry-season day may not be traded for a rainy-season day.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the dry days count as one. All the rainy days count as one. A person may not say to his friend: Plow with me in the dry season, and I will plow with you in the rainy season.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is dealing with two people who trade days of work. It allows the trade inside one season but forbids trading a dry-season day for a rainy-season day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside one season the days are treated as equal, so small differences between them do not matter. A day of plowing in the rainy season is worth more than one in the dry season. If you get a cheaper day now and pay back with a more valuable day later, you are paying back more than you got, and that is like רבית.

keyTerms.meaning: The dry season, when no rain falls
The rainy season, when the ground is soaked
Interest, an extra payment for a loan, which the תורה forbids

steps.confusionAlert: No money is lent here, yet the trade can still be רבית. Trading favors of work counts as a kind of loan, and paying it back with something worth more is forbidden.

phrases.english: All the dry days count as one.
phrases.notes: He means any dry-season day can be swapped for any other dry-season day, as if they were all the same.

phrases.english: All the rainy days count as one.
But he may not say to him:
Plow with me in the dry season
and I will plow with you in the rainy season.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's case of neighbors swapping work days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Work days may be swapped within one season, but a dry-season day may not be repaid with a rainy-season day.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: interest given before the loan or after it
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל teaches that a gift given to win a future loan, or given as thanks after a loan is repaid, is still רבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says: There is early interest and there is late interest. How so? Someone hoped to borrow from his friend, and he sent him a gift and said: This is so that you will lend to me. That is early interest. Someone borrowed from his friend and paid back the money, and then he sent him a gift and said: This is for your money that sat unused with me. That is late interest.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל widens the איסור of רבית. It applies even outside the time of the loan itself, both before the loan starts and after it is fully paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think רבית only means paying extra while the loan is still open. רבן גמליאל says that what matters is the reason for the gift. If it is given because of the loan, it is רבית, even if it comes before the loan or after the repayment.

keyTerms.meaning: Early interest, given before the loan
Late interest, given after the loan is repaid
He had his eye on it, meaning he hoped to

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that רבית depends on the link between the gift and the loan, not only on when the gift is given.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says:
There is early interest
and there is late interest.
How so?
If he hoped to borrow from him,
and he sends him a gift and says:
This is so that you will lend to me,
this is early interest.

phrases.aramaic: לָוָה הֵימֶנּוּ וְהֶחְזִיר לוֹ אֶת מְעוֹתָיו,
phrases.english: If he borrowed from him and paid back his money,
and he then sends him a gift and says:
This is for your money, which sat unused with me,
this is late interest.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: יֵשׁ רִבִּית מוּקְדֶּמֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from work swaps to gifts given around a loan.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gift given because of a loan, whether before it or after repayment, is forbidden as רבית.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: interest paid with words
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון teaches that a borrower may not even pay the lender back with useful information.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: There is interest paid with words. The borrower may not say to the lender: Know that so-and-so has come from such-and-such a place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון takes רבית one step further. Even a favor made only of words, such as passing on helpful news, can count as רבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to here רבית meant giving money, gifts, or work. רבי שמעון says that any benefit the borrower gives because of the loan counts, even if nothing physical changes hands.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
There is interest paid with words.
The borrower may not say to the lender:
Know that so-and-so has come
from such-and-such a place.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: יֵשׁ רִבִּית דְּבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further kind of רבית beyond רבן גמליאל's gifts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Passing on useful information to the lender because of the loan counts as רבית.

steps.title: Who breaks the איסור in a רבית loan
steps.stepSummary: The lender, borrower, ערב, and witnesses all break a לא תעשה. The חכמים add the scribe.
steps.simpleTranslation: These people break a לא תעשה: the lender, the borrower, the guarantor, and the witnesses. The חכמים say: The scribe also does.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists everyone involved in a רבית loan who breaks a לא תעשה. This sets up the next line, which names the actual פסוקים they break.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The איסור is not only on the lender who takes the extra money. Even the borrower who pays it, and the people who help make the deal happen, are guilty. The חכמים say the scribe who writes the loan document is included too.

keyTerms.meaning: Guarantor, who promises to pay if the borrower does not
Scribe, who writes the loan document

steps.confusionAlert: The borrower is the one losing money, yet he also breaks the איסור. רבית is forbidden to give as well as to take.

phrases.english: And these break a negative commandment:
the lender and the borrower,
and the guarantor and the witnesses.
And the Rabbis say: also the scribe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the kinds of רבית to the people who are guilty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All parties to a רבית loan break a לא תעשה; according to the חכמים this includes the scribe.

steps.title: The five פסוקים that are broken
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists five לאוים that the people in a רבית loan break.
steps.simpleTranslation: They break the איסור of 'Do not give,' of 'Do not take from him,' of 'Do not be to him like a creditor,' of 'Do not place interest on him,' and of 'Do not put a stumbling block before the blind, and you shall fear your God, I am ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the list from the previous line by naming the five פסוקים that are broken in a רבית loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not everyone breaks all five. Each one breaks the לאוים that fit his role in the loan. The last one, לפני עור, is about causing someone else to sin. The גמרא in Step 7 explains who breaks which לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of, under the איסור of
Creditor, someone who presses for payment
Before the blind, the איסור of making someone else sin

steps.whatToRemember: רבית covers more than extra money during a loan: work of greater value, gifts before or after, and even helpful words. Everyone involved in the deal is guilty, through five different לאוים.

phrases.english: They break the command 'You shall not give',
and 'Do not take from him',
and 'Do not be to him like a creditor',
and 'Do not place interest upon him',
and 'And before the blind do not put a stumbling block,
and you shall fear your God; I am the Lord.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the פסוקים broken by the people listed in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those involved in a רבית loan break five לאוים: לא תתן, אל תקח, לא תהיה לו כנושה, לא תשימון עליו נשך, and לפני עור.

steps.title: Even a greeting can be interest
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי derives from a פסוק that a borrower who never used to greet the lender first may not start doing so because of the loan. Even words can be רבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון בן יוחי says: Where do we learn that if someone owes his friend a מנה, and he was never used to greeting the lender first, he is now forbidden to greet him first? The פסוק says: 'Interest of any thing (דבר) that is lent with interest.' Even speech (דיבור) can be forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a ברייתא that pushes the idea of the משנה even further. Even a friendly greeting can be forbidden רבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says רבית of 'any דבר.' רבי שמעון בן יוחי reads דבר as connected to דיבור, which means speech. A greeting the borrower gives only because of the loan is a small payment for the loan, so it counts as רבית.

keyTerms.meaning: A lender, someone who is owed money

steps.confusionAlert: The נושה is the lender. The one who may not start greeting is the borrower, who would be 'paying' the lender with words.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבית is not only about money. Any benefit the borrower gives because of the loan can be forbidden.

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says:
From where do we know, for one who is owed a maneh by his friend,
and the borrower is not used to greeting him first,
that it is forbidden to greet him first?
The verse teaches:
"Interest of any thing that is lent with interest":
phrases.notes: דברים 23:20. The word דבר, 'thing,' is being read as דיבור, 'speech.'

phrases.english: even speech is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the משנה's ideas of רבית given before or after a loan and of useful information as payment (Steps 2-3) all the way to a simple greeting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A borrower may not start greeting the lender first if he did not do so before the loan. Even speech can be רבית.

steps.title: Who breaks which prohibition
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains the משנה's list. The מלוה breaks all the לאוים. The לוה breaks three. The ערב and the עדים break only 'do not place interest upon him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And these break the לאו.' אביי says: The lender breaks all of them. The borrower breaks 'Do not lend with interest to your brother,' 'And to your brother do not lend with interest,' and 'Do not put a stumbling block before the blind.' The guarantor and the witnesses break only 'Do not place interest upon him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about who breaks the לאוים. אביי then sorts out exactly which לאו each person breaks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed five לאוים and several people but did not say who breaks which one. אביי assigns them: the lender breaks every one. The borrower breaks the two לאוים of 'לא תשיך' because he lets his brother lend with interest, and he also breaks לפני עור. The ערב and עדים only help set up the interest, so they break just 'לא תשימון עליו נשך.'

keyTerms.meaning: A guarantor, who promises to pay if the borrower does not
Before the blind. This is the לאו against causing another person to sin.

steps.whatToRemember: The lender breaks all five לאוים. The borrower breaks three. The guarantor and witnesses break only one.

phrases.english: "And these violate":
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from Step 4.

phrases.english: Abaye says:
The lender violates all of them.
The borrower violates because of
"Do not lend with interest to your brother,"
phrases.notes: דברים 23:20. Here it is read as 'do not cause your brother to lend with interest.'

phrases.english: "and to your brother you shall not lend with interest,"
and "Before the blind do not place a stumbling block."
The guarantor and the witnesses do not violate
anything except "Do not place interest upon him."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה's list of people (Step 4) and its five לאוים (Step 5), and matches each person to his לאוים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מלוה breaks all the לאוים. The לוה breaks 'לא תשיך' twice and לפני עור. The ערב and עדים break only 'לא תשימון עליו נשך.'

steps.title: Interest lenders lose more than they gain
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון teaches that lenders of רבית end up losing more than they earn. Worse, their actions mock משה רבינו and the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון says: Those who lend with interest lose more than they gain. Not only that, but they make משה רבינו out to be 'wise' and his תורה 'true.' They say: If משה רבינו had known there was profit in this, he would not have written it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about how bad lending with רבית is. The lender's profit is not real, and he is also making fun of the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lender thinks he is earning money, but רבי שמעון says he will lose more than he gains. 'Wise' and 'true' are a polite way of saying the opposite. By acting as if the תורה forbade רבית only because משה did not see the profit, these lenders mock משה and his תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Not only that, but even more

steps.confusionAlert: 'They make משה wise and his תורה true' does not praise them. It is a polite way of saying they mock משה and the תורה.

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Shimon says:
Those who lend with interest
lose more than they gain.
And not only that, but

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמְּשִׂימִים מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ חָכָם וְתוֹרָתוֹ אֱמֶת.
phrases.english: they make Moses our teacher out to be wise and his Torah true.
phrases.notes: This is said politely, but he means the opposite: they treat משה and his תורה as foolish.

phrases.english: And they say:
Had Moses our teacher known
that there would be profit in this matter,
he would not have written it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: מַלְוֵי רִבִּית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After listing the לאוים that the lender breaks, the גמרא adds how harmful and disrespectful his sin is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lenders of רבית lose more than they gain, and they mock משה רבינו and the תורה.

steps.title: Don't walk in front of a borrower who can't pay
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי derives from 'לא תהיה לו כנשה' that a lender who knows the borrower cannot pay may not even pass in front of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: Where do we learn that if someone is owed a מנה by his friend, and he knows the friend does not have the money, he is forbidden to pass in front of him? The פסוק says: 'Do not be to him like a creditor.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about loans in general. A lender must not make a borrower who cannot pay feel pressured, even without saying a word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even without asking for the money, just showing up in front of the borrower reminds him of the debt and makes him uncomfortable. The פסוק 'Do not be to him like a creditor' forbids acting in a way that makes him feel the lender's pressure.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came, usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל
To pass in front of him
Like a creditor who presses for payment

steps.whatToRemember: The תורה protects a poor borrower's feelings too. The lender may not even remind him of the debt by walking past him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the rules of lending cover more than money. They also cover not embarrassing or pressuring a borrower who cannot pay.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
From where do we know, for one who is owed a maneh by his friend,
and he knows that the friend does not have the money,
that he is forbidden to pass in front of him?
The verse teaches: "Do not be to him like a creditor."

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר: מִנַּיִן לַנּוֹשֶׁה בַּחֲבֵירוֹ מָנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבית to a general rule about how a lender must treat a borrower who cannot pay.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lender who knows the borrower cannot pay may not pass in front of him, because of 'לא תהיה לו כנשה.'

steps.title: Pressuring a poor borrower is like a double punishment
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי and רבי אסי say that a lender who pressures a borrower who cannot pay is like someone who sentences him to two punishments, fire and water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי and רבי אסי both say: it is as if the lender sentenced the borrower to two punishments, as the פסוק says, 'You let men ride over our heads; we went through fire and through water.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second voice to רב דימי's teaching about a lender who keeps showing himself to a borrower who cannot pay. רבי אמי and רבי אסי describe how serious this is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי gave the rule: do not even pass in front of the borrower. Here רבי אמי and רבי אסי explain the weight of it. The פסוק describes someone in control 'riding over' others and putting them through fire and water, and that is how the borrower feels.

keyTerms.meaning: You let men ride over our heads

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi, who both say
it is as though he sentenced him to two punishments,
as it is said: 'You have made men ride over our heads,
we came through fire and through water.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second teaching to רב דימי's ruling about not pressuring a borrower who cannot pay.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pressuring a borrower who cannot pay is like putting him through two punishments.

steps.title: Lending without witnesses puts a stumbling block before the borrower
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that anyone who lends money without witnesses violates 'do not place a stumbling block before the blind.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: anyone who has money and lends it without witnesses violates 'Before the blind do not place a stumbling block.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: lending money with no witnesses. רב says this is an actual איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no witnesses, the borrower is tempted to deny the loan. That makes the lender the one who 'places the stumbling block,' so he is guilty of לפני עור.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not place a stumbling block before the blind

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Anyone who has money
and lends it without witnesses

phrases.aramaic: עוֹבֵר מִשּׁוּם ״וְלִפְנֵי עִוֵּר לֹא תִתֵּן מִכְשֹׁל״.
phrases.english: violates 'And before the blind you shall not place a stumbling block.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the רבית and pressure topic to a new loan topic: witnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lending without witnesses violates לפני עור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical rule that loans should be made in front of witnesses or with a written document.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the lender brings a curse on himself
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש gives a different reason against lending without witnesses: the lender brings a curse upon himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: he brings a curse on himself, as the פסוק says, 'Let the lying lips be silenced, that speak arrogantly against the righteous.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a second view about lending without witnesses. He focuses on the harm to the lender himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב looked at the borrower's temptation. ריש לקיש looks at the lender: if he demands money with no proof and the borrower denies it, people will see the lender as a liar and curse him.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
He brings a curse upon himself,
as it is said: 'Let the lying lips be silenced,
that speak arrogantly against the righteous.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second reason, next to רב's, why lending without witnesses is wrong.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lender without witnesses causes people to curse him.

steps.title: רב אשי tests רבינא with a Friday loan request
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן tell רב אשי that רבינא keeps every teaching of the Sages. רב אשי sends him an urgent loan request late on Friday afternoon.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to רב אשי: רבינא keeps everything the Sages said. רב אשי sent to him late Friday afternoon: Please send me ten זוז, because I have a chance to buy a small piece of land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story connected to the rule about witnesses. This step sets up the test, and the next steps show how רבינא responds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Friday afternoon is a rushed time, and the person asking is the great רב אשי himself. If רבינא would ever skip witnesses, it would be now.

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Rav Ashi:
Ravina fulfills
everything that the Rabbis said.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ בַּהֲדֵי פַּנְיָא דְּמַעֲלֵי שַׁבְּתָא:
phrases.english: He sent to him toward evening on Friday:
phrases.notes: "He" is רב אשי, sending to רבינא.

phrases.english: Let the master send me ten zuz
for a small piece of land has come my way to buy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a story that shows the witness rule being kept.

steps.title: רבינא asks for witnesses and a document
steps.stepSummary: Even under pressure, רבינא replies that רב אשי should bring witnesses so they can write a loan document.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent back to him: Let the master bring witnesses, and we will write a document.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the request by insisting on witnesses and a written document. This sets up רב אשי's surprised reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא keeps רב's rule from step 11 even with a great Torah scholar on a rushed Friday. He goes further and asks for a written document, not just witnesses.

phrases.english: He sent to him: Let the master bring witnesses
and we will write a document.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבינא's response to the test.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even for a trusted scholar, a loan needs witnesses and a document.

steps.title: רב אשי asks: even for me?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי pushes back: do I also need witnesses? Do you suspect even me?
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent back to him: Even me too?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges רבינא's demand. He asks whether the rule really applies to someone as trustworthy as himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumes the reason for witnesses is fear that the borrower will cheat. If so, a great and honest scholar should not need them.

phrases.english: He sent to him: Even me too?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבינא's insistence on witnesses.
steps.kashyaTarget: Requiring witnesses from a trustworthy borrower like רב אשי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If witnesses are only needed because a borrower might lie, an honest scholar should be exempt.

steps.title: All the more so for a busy scholar who may forget
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that a scholar needs witnesses even more, because he is busy with learning and may forget. Then the lender ends up cursed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent back to him: All the more so the master, who is busy with his learning, might forget, and I would bring a curse on myself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers רב אשי's challenge. The concern is not dishonesty but forgetting, and a busy scholar is more likely to forget.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא changes the reason behind the rule. The worry is an honest mistake, not cheating. If רב אשי forgot the loan, רבינא would look like a liar, which is exactly ריש לקיש's curse from step 12.
steps.whatToRemember: Witnesses are needed even with an honest borrower, because people forget. A scholar who is busy with learning needs them even more.

phrases.english: He sent to him: All the more so the master,
who is busy with his learning, would forget
and I would bring a curse upon myself.
phrases.notes: Literally "brings a curse on himself." רבינא means himself, using ריש לקיש's words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the reason for the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Witnesses are only needed to guard against a dishonest borrower.
steps.terutzMaskana: Witnesses also guard against honest forgetting, which is even more likely with a busy scholar.

steps.title: Three who cry out and are not answered
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists three people whose cries are not answered: one who lends without witnesses, one who acquires a master for himself, and one whose wife rules over him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: three people cry out and are not answered. They are: one who has money and lends it without witnesses, one who buys a master for himself, and one whose wife rules over him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the theme. Someone who lends without witnesses is one of three people who caused their own trouble, so their cries go unanswered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a new point to רב and ריש לקיש. When the lender later cries out about his lost money, he gets no help, because he brought the loss on himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Cry out and are not answered
One who acquires a master for himself

steps.whatToRemember: Lending without witnesses is an איסור (לפני עור), it brings a curse on the lender, and his cries for help go unanswered.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה צוֹעֲקִין וְאֵינָן נַעֲנִין,
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: Three cry out and are not answered,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מָעוֹת
phrases.english: and these are they: one who has money
and lends it without witnesses,
and one who acquires a master for himself,
and one whose wife rules over him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה צוֹעֲקִין וְאֵינָן נַעֲנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that strengthens the warning against lending without witnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who lends without witnesses is among those who cry out and are not answered.

steps.title: What does 'acquiring a master for himself' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא meant by one who acquires a master for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who 'acquires a master for himself': what is that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the second person in the ברייתא from Step 17 and asks what that unclear phrase means. This sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first and third cases in the ברייתא are easy to picture. 'Acquiring a master for himself' is vague, so the גמרא needs to define it before moving on.

keyTerms.meaning: Acquires a master for himself, putting himself under someone else's control
What is it? A request to define a term

phrases.english: One who acquires a master for himself, what is it?
phrases.notes: This is the second of the three people from the ברייתא we just learned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the middle case in the ברייתא of Step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of person counts as 'one who acquires a master for himself'?

steps.title: Three explanations of acquiring a master
steps.stepSummary: Three opinions: he falsely puts his property in a gentile's name, he gives his property to his children while still alive, or he has bad luck in his town and refuses to move.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: he attributes his property to a gentile. Some say: he writes his property over to his children during his lifetime. Some say: things go badly for him in this town, and he does not go to another town.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives three different answers to its question. Each one describes a man who brings trouble on himself through his own choices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first, he gives the gentile a claim on his property. In the second, he becomes dependent on his own children. In the third, he stays stuck in his bad situation when he could leave. Each time he made his own master, so his cries go unanswered.

keyTerms.meaning: Attributes his property to a gentile, claiming it belongs to him
One who writes his property over to his children

steps.whatToRemember: All three explanations share one idea: a person who puts himself under someone else's power, or into a bad situation he could avoid, has 'acquired a master'.

phrases.english: There are those who say: one who attributes his property to a gentile.
phrases.notes: He falsely says his things belong to the gentile, and that can end up giving the gentile a real hold on them.

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: הַכּוֹתֵב נְכָסָיו לְבָנָיו בְּחַיָּיו.
phrases.english: There are those who say: one who writes his property over to his children in his lifetime.

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: דְּבִישׁ לֵיהּ בְּהָא מָתָא
phrases.english: There are those who say: one who has bad fortune in this town
and does not go to a different town.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18 with three opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three opinions: falsely putting his property in a gentile's name, giving his property to his children during his lifetime, or staying in a town where he has bad luck.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing איזהו נשך
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the chapter איזהו נשך.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, איזהו נשך.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the chapter איזהו נשך. It is a closing line, and nothing is argued here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional promise to come back and learn the chapter again. It tells the learner that the topic of interest and loans in this chapter is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. The formula said at the end of a chapter
The name of the fifth chapter of בבא מציעא, about interest

phrases.english: We will return to you, Eizehu Neshekh

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final teaching in Step 19.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter איזהו נשך is complete.

steps.title: Workers who deceive each other only have a complaint
steps.stepSummary: The new chapter opens: if hired workers and the employer misled one another, there is only a grievance and no money claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who hires artisans, and they deceived one another, they have nothing against one another except a grievance.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a משנה about hiring workers. Its first rule is that when one side misleads the other, the wronged side can complain but cannot collect money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually no real money was lost yet, for example when a deal falls through before work starts. So the משנה gives only a moral complaint (תרעומת), not a court claim.

keyTerms.meaning: A grievance or complaint with no money owed

steps.confusionAlert: 'Each other' includes the employer and the workers. It is not only workers fooling other workers. Either side may have misled the other.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who hires artisans
and they deceived one another –

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לָהֶם זֶה עַל זֶה אֶלָּא תַּרְעוֹמֶת.
phrases.english: they have nothing against one another but a grievance.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַשּׂוֹכֵר אֶת הָאוּמָּנִין וְהִטְעוּ זֶה אֶת זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new chapter השוכר את האומנין after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the employer and workers mislead each other, there is only a grievance and no monetary claim.

steps.title: When backing out causes a loss, the employer may act
steps.stepSummary: If workers back out of a job where delay causes a loss and no one else is available, the employer may hire others at their expense or trick them into coming back.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he hired a donkey driver or a potter to bring posts or flutes for a bride or for the dead, or workers to take his flax out of the soaking tub, or anything that will be lost, and they backed out: in a place where there is no one else, he may hire others at their expense or deceive them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives an exception to the first rule. When the job cannot wait and the loss is real, the employer is not limited to complaining.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wedding or funeral items are useless after the event, and flax left too long in the soaking water gets ruined. In such cases, if no other workers can be found, he may hire replacements and charge the first workers. He may also promise them extra pay to come back and later not pay it.

keyTerms.meaning: Posts or poles, such as for a canopy
The tub of water where flax is soaked
A matter where delay causes a loss
He hires others at their expense

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the rule that workers may not back out of a job where it causes an irreversible loss. The concept דבר האבד is discussed widely in the laws of workers.

phrases.english: If he hired the donkey driver and the potter
to bring posts and flutes
for a bride or for the dead,
or laborers to bring up his flax from the soaking tub,
or any matter that will be lost, and they reneged,
in a place where there is no other person –
he may hire at their expense, or deceive them.
phrases.notes: 'Deceive them' means he may promise them more money to return and then pay only the original wage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to Step 21: where there is a real loss, the employer can do more than complain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a case of loss, where no replacements are available, the employer may hire others at the workers' expense or deceive them into returning.

steps.title: Workers who quit midway are at a disadvantage
steps.stepSummary: If hired workers back out in the middle, they get the worse end of the deal.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who hires artisans, and they backed out: their hand is on the bottom.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a related rule about workers who quit partway through the job. In any dispute over payment, the outcome goes against them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Their hand is on the bottom' means the workers carry the cost of quitting. They cannot leave the employer with a loss, and the payment is figured in the way that is worse for them.

keyTerms.meaning: Their hand is on the bottom. They lose out

steps.whatToRemember: The opening משנה has three levels. Misleading with no real loss gives only a complaint. Backing out where there is a loss lets the employer hire replacements at the workers' expense or trick them into returning. Quitting midway puts the workers at the lower hand.

phrases.english: One who hires artisans and they reneged –
they are at a disadvantage.
phrases.notes: Literally, 'their hand is on the bottom'. In a payment dispute, the outcome goes against them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a further rule about workers who back out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Workers who back out of a job midway are at a disadvantage.
